viewHypothesisPolicy.generationContract: Preserve the exact object identity, proportions, parts, materials, and scale; generate only the named unseen view on a neutral background; do not redesign or add parts.

objectClass.notes: One isolated dorsal view clearly shows the four-wing silhouette and characteristic orange/black/white pattern. Underside, depth, and small appendage joints are not observed.

reasoning: Complex is warranted by four independent wing pivots, compound wing markings, venation, segmented anatomy, six legs, antennae, and animated attachment correctness.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Use only the depth needed to preserve the visible identity and intended behavior.

specializedRegions.notes: No human face or hand regions are present; insect head landmarks are handled by body-anatomy.

surfaceTopologyPlan.reason: Articulation boundaries and thin membranes require separate assemblies; small markings and veins are surface relief/material systems.
surfaceTopologyPlan.decisionRule: Classify each visible system as continuous sculpt, intentional assembly, conforming shell, embedded relief, host-bound fiber, or material-only before modules.

groups.separationReason: Each observed wing has a real thoracic articulation boundary and must rotate independently.
groups.rationale: Four separately hinged membranes preserve the observed silhouette and required runtime motion.
These scale-color regions do not change the primary wing silhouette; runtime may realize them as shallow decals.
Observed veins are sub-silhouette dark linework represented as shallow render detail.

groups.separationReason: Observed exoskeletal regions have recognizable boundaries and different segment behavior.
groups.rationale: Named masses support anatomy hotspots while remaining visibly connected.

groups.separationReason: Appendages attach at anatomical sockets and remain distinct narrow structures.
groups.rationale: Curve-based tubes are bounded approximations of visible appendages and their hidden roots.
Dense setae are bounded to roughness and color breakup rather than unsupported strand grooming.

definitionOfDone: Dorsally, the model reads immediately as Danaus chrysippus: broad orange forewings with black apices and white bands, rounded orange hindwings with black-and-white margins, a narrow dark segmented body, and four independently hinged wings. Wing roots remain attached throughout a subtle asynchronous flight-idle animation.

assumptions: The supplied generated dorsal plate is planning/reference evidence, not proof of unseen biological surfaces.
Right/left wing planforms are mirrored for runtime stability; minor surface marks vary deterministically.
Wing membranes use small visible thickness and double-sided materials for robust browser rendering.
Hidden ventral coloration and appendage insertions are approximate.

coordinateFrame.scaleReference: body length 2.35 model units; full open wingspan approximately 5.2 units

silhouette.boundingShape: broad bilateral four-lobed wing envelope around a narrow longitudinal body
silhouette.symmetry: strong bilateral symmetry about X=0 with small biological/material variation only
dominantCurves: forewing leading edges sweep outward and posterior before rounded dark apices
hindwings form broad convex fans tapering into thoracic roots
negativeSpaces: narrow V between forewing leading edges and antennae
shallow clefts between forewing and hindwing trailing edges
clear gaps between abdomen and hindwing inner edges

observations: Dorsal forewings are warm orange centrally, with dark brown-black apical fields and a transverse series of large cream-white spots.
Rounded hindwings carry broad black marginal bands punctuated by small white spots and two small black discal marks.
The head and thorax are black with paired white spots; the abdomen is narrow, dark brown, segmented, and tapers posteriorly.
Antennae are long, clubbed, and diverge symmetrically; legs are mostly occluded by the body and wings.
Forewings have long convex leading edges, rounded black apices, and orange centers.
Hindwings are broad and rounded with dark cream-spotted margins.
All four roots disappear beneath the thoracic mass.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Measure first; optimize without removing reference-critical features.

proceduralStrategy: Add only the structure required by complexity.
Validate material, surface, lighting, and contact shadow together.
Run interaction and performance checks only when relevant.
risks: Thin layered wing fields can z-fight; each marking layer requires a deliberate dorsal offset.
Four animated wing roots can expose gaps unless membrane shapes overlap the thorax sockets.
Single-view evidence cannot validate side depth, underside markings, or exact leg articulation.
Dense spot and vein geometry can inflate draw calls; repeated markings share geometry and materials where practical.
